stimulus.text: The photograph shows Powell's Mound at Cahokia, near present-day St. Louis, Missouri. Cahokia was the largest city of the Mississippian culture, reaching its height around 1100 to 1200, centuries before European contact. Its people built large earthen mounds, farmed maize, and traded across the Mississippi River valley.
stimulus.source_note: Photograph from the shared image pool; U.S. Army Air Service photograph, public domain.

stem: Which comparison does the evidence about Cahokia best support?

options.text: Cahokia copied the design of European forts built after 1607.
Mound building at Cahokia ended because Cahokia was cut off from all trade.
Indigenous peoples built large permanent centers, as complex societies did elsewhere.
The mounds prove that Cahokia was governed as a Spanish colony.

instruction: Pick one option from the stimulus and stem only. Do not open the question file.
